originality.rationale: The assessed theorem is the exact path-entropy production for every ring N>=4 with strong independent directional coupling K>J, its stationary nearest-neighbor lag-slope identity and its unique thermodynamic temperature optimum. Godrèche 2011 gives an earlier Gibbs-invariant directed model with bounded bias, but not this strong-coupling dissipation theorem; the 2024 complete model solves correlations, not the entropy rate or temperature optimum. A three-spin entropy SCGF in the accessible claim ledger is a strict small-N special case and is not itself claimed new. Parallel-update and Gaussian-spin entropy formulas do not imply the specific single-site binary model law. Residual unindexed-publication risk persists.
residual_risks: The 2011 rate formulas together with standard path-entropy definitions may yield part of the finite-size expression by straightforward computation; novelty rests mainly on strong independent-coupling domain, temporal relation and sharp global temperature optimization.
Unindexed or inaccessible equivalent prior mathematical work may exist; no independent publication-priority determination.
The 2018 Gaussian-chain full text was not inspected, although its state and dynamics are different.

value.rationale: The natural finite-ring EPR is invisible in the fully equilibrium-form stationary spin distribution, but directly measurable from a signed short-lag correlation. The exact N>=4 formula and strict one-maximum thermal law for strongly directional couplings quantify an experimentally interpretable competition between biased updates and the suppression of domain walls; neither a generic textbook local check nor a sample parameter calculation suffices. The global K/J monotonicity and sharp endpoints are substantive, physically motivated structure.
